front.title: Alternative Timestamp Extension Field for NTP Version 5

abstract.t: This document describes an alternative timestamp extension field to the Monotonic Receive Timestamp Extension Field defined in Network Time Protocol version 5 (NTPv5). This extension field is designed to facilitate the transfer of frequency offset information between NTP peers.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Network Time Protocol version 5 (NTPv5) defines various extension fields to carry additional information between NTP peers. The Monotonic Receive Timestamp Extension Field is one such field that provides monotonic timestamp information.

This document specifies an alternative timestamp extension field that is specifically optimized for transferring frequency offset information, which is essential for accurate time synchronization in certain deployment scenarios.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Field Format
section.t: The Alternative Timestamp Extension Field follows the general extension field format defined in NTPv5. The field structure is as follows:

ul.li: Field Type: TBD (to be assigned by IANA)
Length: The total length of the extension field in octets
Frequency Offset: A 32-bit signed integer representing the frequency offset

section.name: Field Semantics
section.t: The Alternative Timestamp Extension Field provides both temporal and frequency information. The timestamp represents the time at which the frequency offset was measured, while the frequency offset value indicates the rate at which the local clock differs from the reference time.

section.name: Usage and Processing
section.t: NTP implementations that support this extension field SHOULD include it in NTP packets when frequency offset information is available and relevant to the peer relationship.
Upon receiving this extension field, NTP implementations MAY use the frequency offset information to improve time synchronization accuracy and stability.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The security considerations for this extension field are similar to those for other NTPv5 extension fields. Implementations MUST ensure that the extension field is authenticated when using NTP's security mechanisms.

Malicious or corrupted frequency offset values could potentially impact clock synchronization accuracy. Implementations SHOULD validate received frequency offset values against reasonable bounds before using them.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests IANA to assign a new extension field type code for the Alternative Timestamp Extension Field from the NTPv5 Extension Field Types registry.
Field name: Alternative Timestamp Extension Field
